articles.title: What is Wobo

lead.v: Wobo is a tutor that explains things live, on your own syllabus, in whichever form the idea needs.

text.v: Ask Wobo anything and the answer arrives the way it should: a board drawn in ink while Wobo talks, a short film you can pause anywhere, a model you can drag, or your own writing marked up. Then practice, and a memory of what did not stick.
Wobo is on every screen. On the home screen Wobo is the conversation; everywhere else it is the small orb in the corner, watching the screen with you and one tap from picking the thing up again.
Four things make Wobo different from a video or a search box:

items.v: It is your syllabus.
You pick your board and class, and Wobo teaches that, chapter by chapter, in its order.
It is made for you, now.
Nothing is pre-recorded. Ask the same question tomorrow and you get a different answer, often in a different form.
Drawing is one part of it.
Wobo also films, simulates, speaks, sets practice, remembers what you missed and writes the Sunday note home.
Every number is checked before it is shown.
The maths is computed and verified by code, not remembered. If a check fails, Wobo redoes it or tells you.

text.v: Wobo is free to use, every day, with an allowance of questions that refills once a day. Pro and Max raise that allowance; the free tier is a real product, not a trailer.

articles.title: Your first five minutes

lead.v: Sign in, tell Wobo what you are studying, and Wobo teaches you one real thing before asking you for anything else.

text.v: Here is the whole of it.

items.v: Sign in.
With your phone number or an email address. Your name comes across with the account, so Wobo knows what to call you.
Tell Wobo what you are studying right now.
Type it, say it, or take a photo of your textbook page or timetable. Something like "class 9 CBSE, we are on quadrilaterals" is plenty.
Confirm your board and class.
Wobo works it out from what you said and shows you one line to tap. If Wobo got it wrong, fix it there.
The first lesson.
Wobo teaches one real thing from what you are actually on this week, on the board, in about two minutes. This is not a demo. It counts.
The tour.
Wobo walks you around the app and points at the real controls: the thread, Learn, Practice, the board, how to circle something and ask about it, how to hold to talk. You try each one as Wobo points.
Three quick questions
so the first analogies land in a world you care about.

text.v: That is it. You never see any of this again; coming back drops you straight where you left off.
If you would rather skip ahead, say "skip the tour" at any point. Nothing breaks.

articles.title: Saying "Hey Wobo"

lead.v: On an adult account, "Hey Wobo" wakes Wobo hands-free. Two words. On a learner account under 18 there is no wake word at all. Hold the orb instead, which works everywhere.

text.v: You do not need it to use Wobo. Tapping the orb or typing works everywhere, and on most screens it is faster.

Where the phrase helps is when your hands are busy: a pen in one hand, a page in the other, a diagram half solved on the screen. Say "Hey Wobo, why is this one negative" and Wobo answers on the screen you are looking at.

items.v: Hold to talk
is the default and always available. Press and hold the orb, or long-press it on a phone, speak, and let go.
On a laptop there is a keyboard shortcut for the same thing, shown in settings.
Wobo is never always-listening for a learner under 18.
The microphone opens when you hold the button and closes when you let go. There is no wake word running in the background on a child's account.
On an adult account you can turn hands-free listening on in settings if you want it. It is off until you do.

text.v: Say it again in fewer words, or type it. Wobo also reads whatever is on the screen, so "why is this negative" usually works better than a long, careful sentence.

articles.title: Talking to Wobo out loud

lead.v: Press and hold the orb, speak, and let go. Wobo answers in voice and draws at the same time.

text.v: Voice is the fastest way to ask about something you are looking at, because you can point with your finger while you talk. Circle the bit you mean and say "this one" and Wobo knows what you mean.
Anything you would say to a teacher beside you. Some that work especially well:

items.v: "Explain this."
"Show me where I went wrong."
"Say it again in terms of cricket."
"Quiz me on this chapter."
"Board" — Wobo brings out the plane and starts drawing on it.
"Slow down", "stop", "go back".

text.v: Interrupting is allowed. Tap, type or speak over Wobo and the pen stops mid-stroke, the same way a person would.

In settings you can change the accent Wobo speaks with, turn narration off so Wobo writes instead of speaks, and turn sound effects off separately. If you turn narration off, Wobo still draws everything; the words appear beside the ink.
Wobo teaches in English first and understands you when you mix in your own language mid-sentence. If Wobo does not follow, say it again in either language and Wobo will keep up.

articles.title: Wobo is a wobot

lead.v: Wobo is not a boy or a girl. Wobo is a wobot, and "Wobo" or "they" is the right way to refer to them.

text.v: People ask, so here is the short answer, once.

Wobo has a body: round, soft, warm-lit, with two eyes and a hand that draws. Wobo has moods you can read at a glance — leaning in when listening, a slow pulse when thinking, a small settle when something lands. None of that is a gender, and none of it is meant to be.
If you ask Wobo directly, Wobo will say so briefly and get back to the problem, because the problem is more interesting.
Why we bother writing this down
Because everything else about Wobo is built for one specific person — your board, your class, your pace, your examples — and a tutor who is nobody in particular is easier for everybody to sit beside.

Wobo is a tutor, not a friend you have to keep. Wobo does not get lonely, does not mind if you disappear for a month, and will not guilt you into coming back. If something serious is going on in your life, Wobo will say plainly that you should talk to an adult you trust, and will help you find the words.

articles.title: What Wobo remembers about you

lead.v: Wobo remembers your board and class, what you have mastered, the mistakes you keep making and the examples you like. You can see all of it and delete any of it.

text.v: Memory is what makes a tutor useful on day forty. Without it, every lesson starts from nothing.

items.v: Your board, class, subjects and any edits you made to your syllabus.
Which topics you have mastered, and whether you did it on your own or with help.
Mistakes worth re-testing, so Wobo brings them back later rather than letting them settle.
The worlds your analogies come from, if you told Wobo what you are into.
Recent conversation, so "do that again with a bigger number" makes sense.
Boards you saved to your notes.

text.v: Ink that Wobo draws on a screen and lets fade is not stored. Voice is used to understand you in the moment and is not kept as a recording. Wobo does not build a profile for advertising, because there is no advertising.
Settings has a memory page. Everything Wobo knows about you is listed there in plain sentences, and each line has a delete next to it. Deleting a line takes effect on your next turn.

Memory works the same way at every age today. There is no consent switch on it yet, so nothing on this page waits for a parent to agree to it, and we would rather tell you that than describe a switch you cannot find. Deleting a line, or erasing what Wobo remembers from settings, is the control you have.

articles.title: Your account and signing in

lead.v: Sign in with an account you already have, or with your phone number. One account carries your board, your progress and your plan across every device.

text.v: Signing in with an account you already have

There is a button for continuing with a Google account. Tap it, choose the account, and you are back here signed in. Wobo asks that account for your name and email address and nothing else: no contacts, no calendar, no files, and nothing is ever posted anywhere on your behalf. A button for continuing with an Apple account is on the same screen; where a way in is not switched on yet, the screen says so under the button rather than letting you tap something that does nothing.
Signing in with your phone number
Enter the phone number you want to use and Wobo sends a code. Enter the code and you are in. There is no password to forget.
In settings, add an email address to an account created with a phone number, or the other way round. Verify it once and either will get you in. This is worth doing before you change phones.
Wobo uses the name on your account when speaking to you. Change it in settings and Wobo uses the new one from the next turn.
Settings, then account. Verify the new one before the old one is removed, so you are never locked out.
Signing out and signing in elsewhere
You can be signed in on several devices at once. Your place, your progress and your saved boards follow you. Signing out on one device leaves the others alone.
Check the number or address for a typo first; almost every failure is that. If a code does not arrive within a minute, ask for another. If you are still stuck, write to
from any address and tell us the number or email you used.

articles.title: Settings

lead.v: Everything you can change about Wobo lives on the You page, reached from the quiet "you" affordance in the top left.

text.v: Which class you are in and which board you follow, with the option of giving Wobo your own syllabus instead. Changing either changes what Wobo teaches from the next lesson on.
On or off. It starts on, so a new learner hears Wobo without going looking for a switch, and one tap turns it off for good. The voice follows the language and country your board is in.
On or off. With it on, everything happens in the same order and with the same timing, it just arrives without the movement.
Auto, light or dark. Auto follows your device. In light, Wobo draws like marker on paper; in dark, like chalk on slate.
Two switches, each on its own. Larger text bumps the type size across the app; high contrast strengthens text and lines.
Festivals we can wish you on
Pick the festivals your family keeps, and Wobo sends a greeting on those days and no others. Pick none and Wobo sends none.
What Wobo remembers about you, and the erase that clears it. What the erase reaches, and what it does not reach yet, is written out in full on the privacy page below.
Send a parent an invite to the Sunday note, see whether they accepted, and end the link in one tap. You can also look at the week the way a parent will see it before you send anything.
Which plan you are on, what its day carries, the date it runs to, and Cancel. Cancelling takes two taps and a plan already ending can be put back in one.

An accent picker, a sound-effects switch separate from the voice, a proactivity dial, a streaks switch, notification switches beyond the festival list, editing your name or your sign-in details, and hands-free listening. None of those is built, and settings will say so until they are.

articles.title: Your privacy and your data

lead.v: We collect what is needed to teach you, we never sell it, and you can see what Wobo remembers and erase it whenever you want.

text.v: Your account details, your board and class, your syllabus edits, your learning history and mastery, your saved boards, and what Wobo remembers about how you learn. Billing details are held by our payment provider, not by us.
We do not sell data. We do not advertise, so there is no profile built for advertisers. We do not use a child's learning data to market to them.

Third-party AI and infrastructure providers process what is needed to run Wobo, under contract, and are not allowed to use it for their own purposes. Your parent sees only what the parent link shows, and only if you or they set it up.
Settings, your data. The memory page lists what Wobo knows about you in plain sentences, line by line.

Settings, your data, erase and start over. It asks once. It clears what Wobo remembers about you, the conversation Wobo was holding, your mastery and progress record, your profile, your mail choices and the parent link, from this device and from your account, and it cannot be undone.
What erase does not reach yet

Your individual answers to practice questions, your ink on the board, your session times, and a syllabus you uploaded yourself. Those are still held, and the account itself, with its email and password, stays open. To have all of that removed, write to support@heywobo.com and ask, and we will do it by hand.
We do not have a button that gives you a file of everything. If you want a copy, write to support@heywobo.com and we will put one together for you.

Everything on this page works the same at every age today. There is no consent switch on memory, voice or photographs yet, and until there is we will not pretend otherwise. A parent can ask for anything on this page on your behalf, at support@heywobo.com.

articles.title: Wobo on your phone, tablet and laptop

lead.v: Wobo works the same on any screen, with a finger, a mouse, a stylus or a keyboard, and everything follows your account.

text.v: The full product in portrait. The plane arrives as a sheet from the bottom instead of a floating panel. Circling something is a finger drag. Holding to talk is a long press on the orb.

Both orientations. If you have a stylus, use it: pressure changes the weight of your ink, your palm resting on the screen is ignored, and drawing your working next to Wobo's is the best way to use the whole thing.

Keyboard shortcuts for everything, including hold to talk and the command palette, which reaches any action in the product. The plane is a floating panel you can move, resize, pin or shrink to a thumbnail with its ink intact.

Every control is reachable and labelled, every practice question has a keyboard path, and everything Wobo draws has a text description that says what the drawing shows, not just that a drawing exists.
Turn it on in settings, or let it follow your device. Everything still draws in the same order with the same timing; it simply appears rather than moves.

Lessons you have opened recently are kept on the device, so a dead network does not end a study session. Asking Wobo something new needs a connection. Anything you did offline syncs when you are back.

articles.title: Ink on your screen

lead.v: For a quick answer, Wobo draws straight onto whatever is already on your screen, and the ink fades when the point is made.

text.v: This is the smallest of the three ways Wobo draws. A ring around the term you asked about. An arrow at the step where it went wrong. A number written beside a slider. One line, in place, on the thing itself.

items.v: The ink is anchored to the actual thing, not to a spot on the glass. Scroll, rotate the phone, switch to dark mode, and the mark stays on its target.
If the thing it points at disappears, the mark fades out rather than floating in space.
It fades on its own once Wobo has finished the sentence. Nothing to dismiss.
Wobo points before saying "this", so the ink is always there by the time the word arrives.

text.v: For a pointer, a correction, one short line. If the answer needs more than a few strokes — a derivation, a diagram from nothing — Wobo brings out the plane instead.

articles.title: The plane

lead.v: The plane is a frosted board that slides out over whatever you are doing, so Wobo can work something out without taking you off the page.

text.v: Say "board", or ask something that needs real working, and the plane arrives from the orb. It is see-through, so the thing you were looking at stays visible underneath.
What you can do with it

items.v: Move it, resize it, pin it.
Drag it where it is not in the way. Pin it and it stays while you scroll.
Shrink it.
It becomes a small thumbnail near the orb with all its ink intact. Tap to bring it back exactly as it was.
Draw on it.
Your strokes and Wobo's share the same surface. Scribble your working and Wobo reads it.
Wipe it.
Say "wipe" or use the eraser. Say "fresh board" and you get a second one; you can have several in a session.

text.v: The plane comes up as a sheet from the bottom. Drag it up for more room, down to shrink it, and it keeps its ink either way.

Anything that takes more than a few strokes: a derivation written out, a graph built from the axes up, a free-body diagram, a molecule drawn in the order a chemist would draw it. Move a slider Wobo has drawn and every number that depends on it is recomputed and rewritten.
The plane's ink stays until you wipe it. Save it to your notes and it is yours permanently.

articles.title: The full board

lead.v: Inside a lesson, the board is the whole screen, and the lesson happens on it.

text.v: There is no page of text with a video at the top. A lesson is Wobo drawing, one idea at a time, while you act on what is drawn.

items.v: One idea per screen. Something to tap, drag, shade or build before it moves on.
Wobo draws and talks together, and pauses when there is something for you to do.
Interrupt whenever you like. Tap, type or speak and the pen stops mid-stroke.
Ask anything mid-lesson. Wobo answers on the same board and picks up where it stopped.
A lesson closes with a boss battle, then the XP.

articles.title: Ask Wobo about anything on the screen

lead.v: Circle it, hold on it, or select it, then ask. Wobo already knows what it is.

text.v: This works on every screen in the app: a lesson, a simulation, a graph, a paused video, a settings page, your own progress chart.

items.v: Circle it.
Drag a loop around it with your finger, mouse or stylus. The loop fades and Wobo has it.
Hold on it.

Select it.
Select text the normal way and ask about the selection.

articles.title: Boss battles

lead.v: A boss battle is the interactive workbook that closes a topic. Finish it and the topic counts as done.

text.v: It is one continuous piece of work rather than a list of questions: a real problem, drawn on the board, that you solve on the same surface, with the parts building on each other.

items.v: Wobo sets it up on the board and steps back.
You work. Write, drag, shade, build, draw your working beside it.
Wobo marks the working, not only the answer, and ink lands on the step that went wrong.
Help is available throughout and does not disqualify anything.
At the end you get Wobo's closing word on how it went and your XP.

text.v: Leave and come back. Your place, your working and your ink are all saved. Nothing is lost and nothing resets.

Once you have a few topics mastered, Wobo builds a bigger one that crosses them, assembled from what you personally know, so it connects things nobody told you were connected. It arrives when you have earned it, not on a schedule.

Beating a boss on your own lights the topic as mastered on your progress page. Beating it with a lot of help lights it as mastered-with-support, which is honest and which is what Wobo uses to decide what to revisit.

articles.title: Streaks, and taking a day off

lead.v: A streak counts the days you showed up. Missing one is fine, and Wobo will never threaten you with losing it.

text.v: A day counts when you do something real: a lesson, a practice run, a boss. Asking Wobo one question counts too. Your day rolls over overnight, on your own clock.

Every week includes a rest day that holds your streak without you doing anything. Use it or do not. Wobo will sometimes suggest resting, and when Wobo does, it is a real suggestion, not a trick to get you back tomorrow.
What you will never see from us

No countdown timer. No message telling you what you are about to lose. No badge taken away for being ill, or busy, or on holiday. If you disappear for a month, Wobo is exactly as pleased to see you when you come back.
At 7, 30, 100 and 365 days, Wobo draws you something. That is the whole reward, plus the XP.
If a streak is the kind of thing that makes you anxious rather than steady, turn it off in settings. Nothing else about Wobo changes and your progress is unaffected.

articles.title: Saving and sharing a board

text.v: Say "save this" or use the save control on the plane or the full board. It goes to your notes with its title, the topic, and the date.

Notes is a tab on the lesson screen, beside the lesson itself. Your kept boards are listed newest first, with the date each was saved, and tapping one draws it again. There is no search and no grouping by subject yet, and the newest twenty-four are the ones kept: save a twenty-fifth and the oldest drops off.

articles.title: The parent link

lead.v: The parent link sends a parent one note a week showing what you actually learnt. You set it up, and you can switch it off.

text.v: A note, once a week: the strengths your work showed, the two or three things worth a nudge, and one line about where the term is heading, in Wobo's words. No marks out of ten, no ranking, and no harsher version of the page you see.

Your conversations with Wobo. Your wrong answers, one by one. A live feed of when you are online. A way to set targets for you. It is a window, not a remote control.

Settings, then the parent link. Enter the parent's email address. They get one invite, and nothing else is sent until they open it and confirm from their own device. If they never confirm, the invite expires and nothing goes to them.

articles.title: Telling us something is wrong

lead.v: If anything Wobo shows you looks wrong, tell Wobo. There is a quiet flag on every screen inside Wobo: press "Tell Wobo", press whichever line fits, and that is the whole thing. A person reads every one of these.

text.v: At the bottom of the rail on a computer, just above the row of doors on a phone, and in the top corner of a full board. It is the same control in all three places, and it already knows which lesson, question or board you were looking at, so you do not have to tell us that part.
You do not have to explain
Six lines, and pressing one sends it. There is a box for your own words underneath and it is optional: a flag with nothing typed in it is a complete report, and nobody will ask you why you sent it.
What to send, if you do want to type something

items.v: What looks wrong, in your own words. One sentence is enough.
Nothing else is needed. The subject, the topic and the screen you were on go with it on their own.

text.v: It goes into a queue a person works through. Anything you mark as upsetting or unsafe goes to the top of that queue and wakes somebody up the moment it arrives.
There is no case number, no turnaround time, and no message back to you when it is settled. Those are not built, and we would rather say so here than let you wait for one.
You can still write to us
support@heywobo.com, any time, and a person answers. Use it if you would rather explain properly, or if you want an answer back.
If you think a question marked you wrong

On an equation practice question there is a control on the question itself: "I think I'm right". Wobo re-checks your answer against the equation, and where the proof is on your side the mark changes and the question is not asked again. That control is on equation practice today, and not yet on every kind of question.
What we do with what you send
We read it, we work out whether the content was wrong, and we fix what was. If we think the content was right, we say why, plainly.

A picture of exactly what you were looking at, drawn by our own renderer; ink and blur tools to mark it up; and a message back to you when a report is settled. All three are things we want and none of them is built.

articles.title: When your syllabus changes

lead.v: When a board publishes a new syllabus, Wobo tells you what moved and asks whether you want to switch. Nothing changes underneath you.

text.v: Each academic year or edition is a separate version. You are pinned to the one you chose, and it never changes after you have started on it. A correction is a new version too, never an edit to the one you are using.

We check the boards' own pages regularly and around the times they usually publish. If the document has changed, Wobo builds the new version, checks it the same way as the first, and then tells you, in one line per change:

items.v: Chapters that were added or removed.
Chapters that moved to a different class.
Topics that were renamed.

text.v: You decide. Switch and your progress carries across, matched chapter by chapter; anything that no longer exists is kept in your history rather than deleted. Your own edits are reapplied, and Wobo tells you if any of them no longer has a home.
Staying on your version is a perfectly good answer, especially mid-year. Wobo will not ask again until the next one.
If a change lands mid-year, Wobo mentions it once, quietly, and does not push. Your exam is on the syllabus your school is teaching, not on the newest document.

lead.v: Nothing is made in advance. When you open a topic, Wobo builds that lesson for you, checks it, and draws it.

text.v: A lesson written once for everybody is written for nobody. Built at the moment you open it, a lesson can use your board's wording, your class's depth, the examples you like, and the things you already know as scaffolding.

articles.title: Prerequisites and gates

lead.v: If a topic needs something you have not done yet, Wobo says so and offers to cover it first. You can always go ahead anyway.

text.v: A gate in Wobo is advice, never a wall. There is no locked padlock and no "complete the previous unit to continue".
One quiet line before you start: what this topic leans on, whether you have it, and a shortcut to the missing piece. Then two doors: cover that first, or carry on.

Every topic is joined to the ideas it depends on. Wobo knows which of those you can do on your own, which you can do with help, and which you have not met. The line you see is built from that, not from whether you clicked through a unit.

If you do go ahead, Wobo teaches the new thing using only ideas you have actually mastered as the stepping stones. Same destination, different route, built for what you personally know. That is often better than going back.
